label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness score (1.74), PHQ-9 depression score (1.75), and GAD-7 anxiety score (2.17) all sit in the higher range, suggesting a pattern of co-occurring emotional distress. With 165 respondents in this cluster, it reflects a substantial subgroup where extended screen time coincides with pronounced psychological burden.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen/internet use exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Extended daily digital engagement (more than 5 hours)
Elevated feelings of loneliness and social disconnection (UCLA-8 mean 1.74)
Notably high anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean 2.17, the most elevated indicator)
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety suggesting compounded emotional distress
High educational attainment yet persistent psychological vulnerability
tone: Strained and quietly overwhelmed — reflecting a population that is accomplished on paper but emotionally burdened, navigating heavy digital immersion alongside significant mental health challenges

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report lower levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms compared to other groups. With UCLA-8 loneliness, PHQ-9 depression, and GAD-7 anxiety scores all well below scale midpoints, these individuals demonstrate generally positive psychological well-being across all three measured dimensions.
demographic_anchor: Male, holding a graduate degree or above, with 1–3 hours of daily screen time or social media use
behavior_markers: Reports minimal loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.77, near the low end of the scale)
Exhibits very low depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.33)
Maintains moderate and limited screen time (1–3 hours daily)
Represents a relatively sizable subgroup (n = 150) suggesting this is a common well-functioning profile

label: Lonely but Emotionally Resilient
summary: This profile captures respondents who report notably elevated loneliness yet maintain relatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Despite feeling socially disconnected, they do not exhibit the emotional distress patterns typically associated with loneliness, suggesting a degree of psychological resilience or effective coping mechanisms that buffer against mood and anxiety disorders.
demographic_anchor: Predominantly female, holding graduate-level or higher education, reporting 1–3 hours of daily screen time or social media use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) indicating moderate-to-high perceived social isolation
Low depressive symptom burden (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.86) suggesting minimal clinical depression
Low anxiety symptom levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.91) indicating limited generalized anxiety
Relatively moderate digital engagement (1–3 hours daily), possibly reflecting deliberate screen-time boundaries
Disconnect between social isolation feelings and affective symptom severity, hinting at cognitive or structural coping strategies
tone: Quietly disconnected yet emotionally stable; introspective rather than distressed
